clue.text: Report of new Oriental combine

indicators.note: new signals that the letters of the following word are made fresh in another order

parts.note: taken as written: the word whose letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: News of a fresh Eastern business group or merger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' is the anagram signal on ORIENTAL; 'combine' looks like a business noun but only links, asking the letters to be put together.
explanation.definitionFit: A relation is a narrative account, as when one gives a relation of events, so it is a kind of report.

clue.text: A log-note amount of wood it comprises!

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
a cord is a measure of cut firewood, 128 cubic feet

explanation.surface: A log on a pile of firewood is part of the stack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it comprises' just links: the answer is made up of the note and the wood measure.
explanation.definitionFit: A record is a written log, as a ship's log records its voyage.

clue.text: There's nothing up with a feature on going straight

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for nothing is written upwards, so backwards

parts.note: nil means nothing
an ear is a feature of the face

explanation.surface: A reformed criminal claims nothing is amiss now he is going straight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going straight' suggests a reformed criminal but simply means in a line.
explanation.definitionFit: Something linear runs in a single line, without curving.

clue.text: The written matter about the queen exhibits some warmth

indicators.note: about means the first pieces go around the royal letter

parts.note: taken as written
MS is short for manuscript, written matter
R is for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A document about the monarch shows a warm tone.
explanation.definitionFit: A therm is a unit of heat, so therms measure some warmth.

clue.text: Not the government's work-place

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
a position is a place

explanation.surface: An office where people work who are not in government.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads 'Not the government is' the answer: the opposition is the party out of power.
explanation.definitionFit: In parliament, those not in power form the opposing side facing the ruling party.

clue.text: Question a social worker indirectly

parts.note: to question is to ask
an ant is a social insect, and many ants are workers

explanation.surface: Asking a welfare worker something in a roundabout way.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'social worker' in crosswords is often an ant or bee, insects living in colonies.
explanation.definitionFit: Askant means sideways or obliquely, so looked at indirectly.

clue.text: Point to quiet attendant brought to a standstill

parts.note: S, south, is a point of the compass
taken as written
p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet
a page is a young attendant

explanation.surface: A hushed servant is made to halt in his tracks.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoppage is a halt, when things come to rest.

clue.text: A learned person ran over unfinished article-such a bloomer!

parts.note: an MA, Master of Arts, is a learned person
taken as written

indicators.note: unfinished means the article loses its final letter

parts.note: the is the definite article in grammar

explanation.surface: A scholar dashed through an incomplete article and made a howler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' looks like a blunder but means a flowering plant; 'over' simply places the pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Amaranth is a flowering plant, so it is a bloomer in the gardening sense.

clue.text: Seeing a fall in sound instruction

indicators.note: in means the fall is placed within the sound

parts.note: a ting is a light ringing sound
rain is a fall from the sky, a rainfall

explanation.surface: Watching a drop in good teaching standards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seeing' only links. 'sound instruction' looks like a phrase meaning good teaching, but 'sound' is the ting and 'instruction' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Training is teaching given to develop a skill.

clue.text: Not in favour of bait being used, so show scorn for it

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
to bait is to tempt or lure

explanation.surface: An angler opposed to using bait looks down on the practice.
explanation.definitionFit: Contempt is disdain, the feeling of looking down on something.

clue.text: Issue a word of thanks for the music

parts.note: issue means offspring, so a son
ta is an informal British word for thank you

explanation.surface: A child says thank you for a piece of music.
explanation.definitionFit: A sonata is a musical composition, usually for one or two instruments.

clue.text: Extremely backward, but raise the greatest number of children

parts.note: to raise children is to rear them
most means the greatest number

explanation.surface: A family that is very old-fashioned yet brings up the largest brood.
explanation.definitionFit: Rearmost means furthest at the back, as backward as possible.

clue.text: Injury can result when gunmen turn round

indicators.note: round means the turn goes around the gunmen

parts.note: a spin is a turn
RA, the Royal Artillery, are gunners in the British Army

explanation.surface: Someone may get hurt when armed men wheel about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can result when' just links. RA, the Royal Artillery, is a crossword staple for gunmen.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprain is a wrenching hurt to a joint's ligaments.

clue.text: The delinquent but macho element

parts.note: macho suggests male
a factor is an element or component

explanation.surface: A youth offender whose swagger is part of the problem.
explanation.definitionFit: A malefactor is a wrongdoer or criminal.

clue.text: This could be shattering to set in order

indicators.note: could be signals the word that follows may be rearranged to give another

explanation.surface: This news may be devastating, so let's tidy up.
explanation.definitionFit: To straighten things is to tidy or arrange them neatly.

clue.text: Top man getting 27 properly organised

indicators.note: properly organised means the letters of the cross-referenced answer are rearranged

parts.note: the answer to 27 across is the lender who is owed money

explanation.surface: The boss gets someone well arranged.
explanation.walkthrough: '27' points to the answer of 27 across, whose letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A director is a top manager on a company's board.

clue.text: The model colours

explanation.surface: A flag carried as the ideal example.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is a model to be followed, and also a flag or banner, a regiment's colours.

clue.text: Manoeuvring when up, as greed's involved

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Climbing the ladder when avarice is at play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when up' means on horseback: the definition describes a horse being put through movements by its rider.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressage is the training of a horse to perform precise moves under its rider.

clue.text: Bury runner-he's not officially entered

parts.note: to inter is to bury
a loper is one who runs with long strides

explanation.surface: Bury is a town, and its runner was an unregistered entrant.
explanation.definitionFit: An interloper is an intruder, someone who comes in without right.

clue.text: Robbed if left in debt

indicators.note: in means the pieces go inside the debt word

parts.note: in the red means in debt
taken as written

explanation.surface: Stolen from if left owing money.
explanation.definitionFit: To rifle is to ransack and steal from, so rifled means plundered.

clue.text: The vicious individual the German turned on first

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above
turned means the German article is read backwards

parts.note: das is a German word for the
1st, written IST, is first

explanation.surface: A cruel person the German attacked first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned on' looks like attacked; 'turned' reverses DAS and 'on' puts that above 1ST, read as IST.
explanation.definitionFit: A sadist is someone who takes pleasure in inflicting cruelty.

clue.text: A book to give the trainee some keenness, right?

parts.note: L is a learner, the trainee driver's plate
edge is sharpness or keenness

explanation.surface: Offering a reading assignment to sharpen the apprentice.
explanation.definitionFit: A ledger is an account book.

clue.text: The man put in to govern Estonia

indicators.note: put in means the letters are lodged inside the next words

explanation.surface: A man appointed to rule a Baltic state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The man' stands for a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernest is a man's first name.

clue.text: Playful repartee only adolescents find acceptable?

explanation.surface: Teen banter grown-ups disapprove of.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word into BAD IN AGE: unacceptable to the mature, so only the young approve.
explanation.definitionFit: Badinage is light teasing banter; read as bad in age, it is something frowned on by older people.

clue.text: Tip-top jewellery!

parts.note: tip-top means first-rate but here means worn at the very top of the head

explanation.surface: Excellent gems!
explanation.definitionFit: Tiaras are jewelled crowns worn on the top of the head.

clue.text: Putting off housing everyone in smart surroundings

indicators.note: in means everyone goes inside the smart word

parts.note: to smart is to sting, here forming the outer part
all means everyone

explanation.surface: Delaying finding homes for people in a fancy neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'housing' looks like the container signal too; it is a link, as 'in ... surroundings' already places ALL.
explanation.definitionFit: Stalling is delaying or playing for time.

clue.text: Look embarrassed about a certain figure study

parts.note: re means about, concerning
D is the Roman numeral for 500
a den is a study or private room

explanation.surface: Blushing over a sum in the study.
explanation.definitionFit: To blush is to go pink in the face from shame.

clue.text: Well-organised 15-one's obliged to him

indicators.note: well-organised means the cross-referenced letters are put in a new order

parts.note: the answer to 15 down is the top manager

explanation.surface: A tidy boss is owed something.
explanation.walkthrough: '15' points to the answer of 15 down, whose letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A creditor is the lender, to whom a debtor owes money.
